questions.q: Fill in the blank space designated by the question mark. [Diagram: Input Signal -> Sensor -> ? -> Actuator -> Output Signal; Sensor and '?' are grouped as the transducer's input side, '?' and Actuator as the transducer's output side]
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'this sensor plus the processor ... this is a transducer. Similarly, actuator plus processor is also a transducer'.

questions.q: What is the maximum data rate of Z-Wave communication technology?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): Z-wave 'data rate is up to offered is up to about 100 kbps' over ~30 m.

questions.q: Which device converts electromagnetic energy into electricity and vice versa?
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'antennas which will convert electromagnetic energy into electrical energy and vice versa'.

questions.q: What does 'Range' indicate in a sensor?
options: The smallest change in input that can be detected
The difference between the standard value and the value produced by the sensor
The highest and the lowest value of the physical quantity within which the sensor can actually sense
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): range 'means the range of operation lowest value to highest value'.

questions.q: Which coding scheme is used by the IEEE 802.15.4 standard for transmitting information?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 'DSSS, the direct sequence spread spectrum coding scheme that is used to transmit information'.

questions.q: What is the standard transmission range of IEEE 802.15.4?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 802.15.4 'range typically is about 10 to 75 meters'.

questions.q: Which low-power radio communication technology was designed as a simpler and cheaper alternative to Zigbee for small to medium-range connectivity?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): 'unlike ZigBee this particular technology Z-wave is simpler and cheaper' for small/medium range.

questions.q: Which organization has developed the ISA 100.11a standard?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): ISA 100.11a 'was developed by international society for automation the ISA'.

questions.q: What communication modes are supported between two NFC devices?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): NFC 'two communication modes are supported ... active active and ... active passive'.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the drawbacks of proprietary non-IP-based solutions?
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): drawbacks of non-IP solutions: limited flexibility to end users, interoperability, limited last mile connectivity.

questions.q: Which MQTT QoS Level is also known as "at most once" delivery?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): 'QoS 0 which is about ensuring at most once delivery'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: In CoRE, the IoT client uses ______ for the discovery of IoT devices.
questions.explanation: Lecture 04 (IoT Networking Part I): 'IoT client uses the lookup interface for discovery of IoT devices'.

questions.q: Apart from MQTT, which IoT networking protocol supports the publish/subscribe framework?
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): XMPP, AMQP and DDS RTPS are all described as publish/subscribe based.

questions.q: Which of the following IoT protocols is based on the session layer of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Corrected after checking the lecture (was: AMQP). Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): the only protocol the lecture calls a session protocol is CoAP: 'CoAP is kind of an application layered protocol ... even more specifically it ensures session, so, session protocol' (Misra's slide: 'CoAP - session layer protocol designed by IETF CoRE'). MQTT/AMQP are described only as pub/sub over TCP; uploaders split AMQP vs MQTT, so moderate confidence.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of RFID?
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): RFID has 3 components - tag, reader, software (antenna is inside the tag); a router is not a component.

questions.q: In the context of Industry 4.0, what is the full form of CPS?
questions.explanation: CPS = Cyber Physical Systems (named in Lecture 06 and Lecture 11).

questions.q: State True or False: Business, providing information goods, has virtually zero transportation and replication cost.
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): 'business providing information goods has virtually zero transportation and replication cost'.

questions.q: Which of the following technologies is used by research scientists to selectively modify the DNA of living organisms?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): biological megatrends: manipulating DNA, 'advanced genetic engineering is a reality'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true about addressing an economic crisis or recession?
options: Observing an increase in prices of major commodities is a key indicator.
Increasing productivity and reducing costs can help recover from a recession.
The main economy of a manufacturing location should always be based on only one resource to avoid crisis.
Recovery from a depression is faster than recovery from a recession when the same solution is applied.
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): in crisis/recession 'reduction in prices ... important to increase the productivity and reduce the overall cost'.

questions.q: What does ERP stand for in the context of ICT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): ICT enables 'Enterprise Resource Planning ERP based systems'.

questions.q: How can enterprises improve sustainability with respect to energy consumption?
options: Increasing usage of non-renewable energy sources
Reducing energy consumption from non-renewable sources and increasing use of renewable energy
Focusing solely on reducing renewable energy costs
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): reduce energy consumption and produce energy from renewable sources like solar, wind.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of "Just-In-Time" in a Lean Production System?
options: Ensuring each process produces what is needed by the next process in a continuous flow
Producing in advance to meet potential future demand
Reducing production costs by purchasing cheap materials
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): JIT 'each process produces what is needed by the next process in a continuous flow'.

questions.q: What is a 'value stream' in a Lean Production System?
options: A set of tools for production
All the actions required for a product from order to delivery
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): 'value streams are all the actions that are required for a product from order ... to the delivery'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of Lean Production in Industry 4.0?
options: Increasing waste in processes to improve flexibility
Focusing on non-value-added activities to reduce costs
Identifying waste in processes and eliminating it
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean in Industry 4.0 includes 'identifying waste in the processes and eliminating them'.

questions.q: Which of the following technologies is a medium for achieving smart and connected systems?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): embedded systems are a key medium for smart and connected products.

questions.q: Which of the following are key attributes of a smart business model?
options: Manual processes, cost reduction, and labor dependency
Value proposition, revenue streams, and technologies
Traditional marketing, fixed costs, and limited innovation
Centralized control, non-digital strategies, and fixed processes
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): key attributes are value proposition, revenue stream and technologies.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of a Smart Factory?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): smart factory components are smart machines, processes, engineering, devices, IT, analytics - not physical ledgers.

questions.q: In the Automation Pyramid of a Smart Factory, which level is just above the Device Level?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): automation pyramid 'device level, then ... the control level, then ... manufacturing system level, and the ERP level' - Control is directly above Device (the 'ERP level' alt copy is wrong).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a prerequisite of the Industrial Internet of Things?
questions.explanation: Not in Weeks 1-2 transcripts; security, interoperability and scalability are IIoT requirements, incompatibility is the opposite of a prerequisite.

questions.q: In which format is healthcare data transmitted to maintain data uniformity and interoperability?
questions.explanation: Not in Weeks 1-2 transcripts; HL7 (Health Level Seven) is the healthcare data interchange standard (covered in the IIoT healthcare lecture).

questions.q: What is the main difference between Embedded Systems and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)?
options: Embedded systems are standalone devices, whereas CPS are networked systems.
CPS have limited resources, while embedded systems are not resource constrained.
Main issues of Embedded Systems are timing and concurrency, while the main issues of CPS are real-time response and reliability.
CPS lack physical components, while embedded systems include them.
questions.explanation: L11: embedded system 'confined to this particular single device'; CPS 'a network set of such kind of embedded systems'. Option C reverses the lecture's issues.

questions.q: What does "reactive computation" in CPS signify?
options: Interaction with the environment in an ongoing manner
questions.explanation: L11: 'reactive computation means ... interaction of the system with the environment in a continuous fashion'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. In healthcare applications, CPS is used for ______.
questions.explanation: L11: 'robotic surgery or image-guided surgery. These are examples of cyber physical systems ... in healthcare'.

questions.q: Which programming language developed in 1958 aided the evolution of Artificial Intelligence?
questions.explanation: L14 mentions Lisp and PROLOG as AI languages; Lisp was created by McCarthy in 1958 (Prolog 1972).

questions.q: Which level in the "5C Architecture" ensures the gathering of precise status information of machines?
questions.explanation: Connection is not offered; in the 5C model the Cyber level is the central hub where information from every machine is gathered to give insight into each machine's status (L11: data 'received at some kind of a hub').

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Intelligent sensors are capable of ______.
options: Processing sensed data and managing external sensors/devices
questions.explanation: L11: intelligent sensors 'are capable of processing sensed data ... capable of managing and controlling external sensors and devices'.

questions.q: What are the five phases of the product lifecycle as per PLM in Industry 4.0?
options: Ideation, Manufacturing, Expansion, Customer Feedback, Upgradation
Requirement Analysis, Development, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance
questions.explanation: L12: phases 'visualize, explain, perceive, use/support, and then dispose/retire'.

questions.q: How many steps are there in the PLM solution approach in Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L12: 'for Industry 4.0, these are the 10 step approaches that can be used for PLM'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a key component of an AR Device?
questions.explanation: L13: AR device components are 'sensors and cameras, projection screen, processing unit, reflection systems like mirrors'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning
Deep Learning is a subset of Artificial Intelligence
Machine Learning is a superset of Artificial Intelligence
Artificial Intelligence is a superset of Machine Learning
questions.explanation: L14: ML is a branch of AI, so 'Machine Learning is a superset of Artificial Intelligence' is the incorrect statement.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a challenge of AI in IIoT?
questions.explanation: L14 AI: 'challenges of AI in IIoT. Connecting different devices, understanding the data, training the data, making it accessible, making ... actionable'. Lack of data is not listed; connecting devices is.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of data preprocessing in Big Data analytics?
options: To remove noises and redundancies before analysis
To generate fake data for testing purposes
questions.explanation: L15: 'The data will have to be pre-processed to remove noise redundancy, inconsistency'.

questions.q: What type of analytics is used to predict future trends based on historical data patterns?
questions.explanation: L15: 'Predictive analytics talks about what is next, what is the pattern'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not one of the primary constraints of mobile CPS?
questions.explanation: Not in the transcripts; mobile CPS are constrained by network stability, power and security; design aesthetics is not a constraint.

questions.q: What are the components of the 5C architecture for CPS?
questions.explanation: L11: 5C = connection, conversion, cyber, cognition, configuration.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of SCADA in industrial applications?
options: Control and monitoring of physical processes
questions.explanation: L19: SCADA is 'an advanced industrial control system' that processes, monitors and analyzes data collected from sites.

questions.q: What is the function of WSANs in industrial processes?
options: Integration of sensors and actuators with wireless networks
questions.explanation: L19: 'a wireless sensor and actuator network in the industry scale connecting different machinery'.

questions.q: What does cybersecurity primarily aim to protect?
options: Internet-connected systems, including hardware, software, and data
questions.explanation: L16: cybersecurity protects internet-connected systems' 'hardware, software and data'.

questions.q: Which industrial sector benefits from advanced analytics using the Industrial Internet?
questions.explanation: L18: industrial internet applications are 'commercial aviation, rail transportation, power production, oil and gas sectors, and healthcare'.

questions.q: Cyber Physical systems comprise which of the following layers?
options: Control Layer, Cognitive Layer, Cyber Layer, Conversion Layer, and Connection Layer
Sensing Layer, Edge Computing Layer, Cloud Layer, Decision-Making Layer, and Execution Layer
Detection Layer, Data Processing Layer, Connectivity Layer, Automation Layer, and User Interaction Layer
Edge Computing Layer, Automation Layer, Detection Layer, Decision-Making Layer, and Device Layer
questions.explanation: L20: 5C layers are connection, conversion, cyber, cognitive and 'finally, the control layer'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a differentiator between IIoT and Automation?
questions.explanation: L17: ubiquitous sensing, advanced analytics and IT tools/methodologies are all differentiators, so 'None of these'.

questions.q: In the context of Cybersecurity for Industry 4.0, what does SDCMA stand for?
options: Secure Data and Cloud Management Architecture
Secure Data and Cloud Management Architecture
questions.explanation: L16: 'software defined cloud manufacturing architecture'.

questions.q: According to GE, ____________ can be defined as "the association of the global industrial system with low-cost sensing, interconnectivity through internet, high-level computing and analytics."
questions.explanation: L18: 'according to GE industrial internet can be defined as the association of the global industrial system, with low cost sensing interconnectivity through internet and high level computing and analytics'.

questions.q: What are the three key elements of the Industrial Internet?
options: Connected Devices, Ubiquitous Sensing, and Cloud Computing
Intelligent Machines, Advanced Analytics, and People at work
5G Networks, Quantum Computing, and Virtual Reality
Autonomous Robots, Blockchain, and Cloud Gaming
questions.explanation: L18: intelligent machines, advanced analytics, people at work.

questions.q: What is Multisensing?
options: Ability to sense multiple parameters at a single sensor node
Using multiple sensors to measure a single parameter
A network of distributed sensors communicating wirelessly
Ability to process sensor data using artificial intelligence
questions.explanation: L19: 'Multi sensing ... sensing multiple parameters ... In a single sensor node'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an advantage of WSANs?
options: Does not require any power source to operate
questions.explanation: L19: WSAN advantages are easy deployment, self-organization, 'pre installed infrastructure' and low cost; needing no power is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major challenge for industrial processes in Industry 4.0?
options: Reduced need for supply chain management
questions.explanation: L20 challenges: dynamic market conditions, 'constrained work force', supply chain, resource utilization, product management.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of an autonomous pull economy in Industrial Process 4.0?
questions.explanation: L20: autonomous pull economy benefit 'end-to-end automation facility'.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the basic components of a SCADA system?
options: Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC) and Remote Terminal Units (RTU)
questions.explanation: L19: SCADA components are supervisory system, HMI, RTU, communication interface, SCADA programming and PLC.

questions.q: According to IEEE 1451 standards, how is a smart sensor defined?
options: Sensor with limited memory and no communication capabilities
Sensor with small memory and standardized physical connection to enable communication with the processor and data network
A basic sensor without processing or networking capabilities
Sensor that only works in standalone mode without network integration
questions.explanation: L19: IEEE 1451 smart sensor has 'small memory and standardized physical connection to enable communication with the processor and data network'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a key sector of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Industry 4.0 sectors include smart robotics, intelligent manufacturing, smart warehousing; paper-based inventory is not one.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of the Outcome-Based Model in IoT business?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): outcome-based model advantages include 'increased customer satisfaction', reduced negotiation cycle, reduced risk, increased profit margin.

questions.q: Which layer in the Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) implements domain-specific applications and decision support systems and provides interfaces to end-users?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'the enterprise layer basically implements domain-specific requirements, decision support systems, and ... interfaces to end-users'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of IIoT business models?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IIoT business model components are 'value proposition, value capturing mechanism, value network, value communication'.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a Cloud-Based Business Model in IIoT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): cloud services offered on demand/subscription (lease of compute, storage); temporary leasing is the fitting purpose.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Based on the leading and lagging Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) indicators, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are also categorized into ______ and ______.
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'leading KPI and lagging KPI are the two different KPI categories for OSH'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four viewpoints in the Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA)?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): the four viewpoints are business, usage, functional and implementation; no financial viewpoint.

questions.q: State true or false. In the Usage Viewpoint of IIRA, "Task" is a basic unit of work carried out by a party assuming a role.
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'the task is a basic unit of work, that is carried out by a party, that assumes a specific role'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a challenge uniquely associated with assetsharing IoT business models?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): asset-sharing challenges include security, mutual arrangements, 'asset configuration', device synchronization; resource utilization/scalability are listed as advantages.

questions.q: What are the key revenue models in a Cloud-Based Business Model?
options: One-time installation charges, Maintenance fees, Donations
Mass production, Bulk discounts, Customer referrals
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): cloud-based revenue model: 'pay-per-use model ... subscription fees, advertisements'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the subscription-based IoT business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): subscription model is predictable and generates recurrent revenues.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are types of business models for IoT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): business models for IoT: subscription, outcome-based, asset-sharing, IoT-as-a-service.

questions.q: What is a major benefit of the layered databus pattern in IIRA?
options: Rapid device-to-device integration with minimal response time
Elimination of automation in industrial systems
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): layered databus allows 'device to device integration with minimum response time'.

questions.q: State true or false. Lack of interoperability, data privacy, security issues, and authentication of data at the organizational level are some of the major challenges of IIoT-based business models.
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): challenges listed include security/data privacy, lack of interoperability, increased complexity/cost, lack of data governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a standard IIoT reference architecture?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): patterns are three-tier, gateway-mediated edge, layered databus.

questions.q: Which industrial communication technology is suitable for hazardous environments?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Profibus PA uses MBP which 'is very useful for hazardous environment'.

questions.q: Which type of modem allows simultaneous bi-directional communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): 'duplex bi-directional and at the same time; that means simultaneously'.

questions.q: Which of the following industrial communication protocols follow a clientserver architecture?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): Modbus TCP 'uses client-server architecture'.

questions.q: What type of tasks is enabled by Smallcell Deployment in cellular networks?
options: Alleviating backhaul burden and reducing latency
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): small cell deployment objectives include 'alleviating burden on the backhaul', energy efficiency, decreasing dead zones.

questions.q: The DS1621 temperature sensor generates how many bits of temperature data?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): DS1621 'will generate 9 bits of temperature data'.

questions.q: Which of the following sensors is used to measure acceleration and provides 3-axis (X, Y, Z) values?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): ADXL335 accelerometer gives X, Y, Z values.

questions.q: Which sensor is used for detecting human presence based on infrared radiation?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): 'PIR sensor basically detect the infrared radiation coming from the human body'.

questions.q: In an MOS gas sensor, what happens to the resistance in an n-type sensor when exposed to a reducing gas?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'In n-type sensors the resistance decreases ... with respect to the baseline resistance when ... exposed to a target gas'.

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics describes a gas sensor's ability to detect a specific gas in the presence of other gases?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'Selectivity is the ability to detect a particular gas in a mixture of different gases'.

questions.q: What is the maximum data transmission range for EtherCat using optical waveguides?
questions.explanation: Not spoken in Lecture 28 (slide detail); EtherCAT spans up to 20 km over optical fibre.

questions.q: Which communication protocol uses Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) over Ethernet?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'Ethernet IP basically happens to be like, CIP over Ethernet'.

questions.q: What is the total bus length supported by Interbus?
options: 24n-2 meters, where n is the number of slaves
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Interbus 'total bus length is 13 kilometres'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key requirement for Industrial communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): industrial communication requires 'very low latency'.

questions.q: How are sensors categorized based on their power requirements?
questions.explanation: Lecture 1 (Sensing & Actuation): sensors 'could be classified as either passive sensor or active sensor' (based on whether they need external power/excitation).

questions.q: Modbus is an industrial communication protocol for Fieldbuses that follows a master-slave architecture. What is the maximum number of slave devices supported by the master node in this protocol?
questions.explanation: Not covered in the lecture; Modbus serial addressing allows 247 slave addresses (1-247).

questions.q: Which of the following topologies is NOT supported by Zigbee?
questions.explanation: 'different topologies that are supported by ZigBee, star topology, tree topology, and mesh topology' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)); the 'Bus' answer in the 2025 copy is wrong.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of Distributed Control Systems (DCS)?
questions.explanation: 'DCs basically provides increased reliability because there is distributed control' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: In which frequency bands do LoRa operate?
questions.explanation: LoRa bands '169, 433, 868 and 915 MHz ... depending on the territory' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which library is required to work with the LoRa?
questions.explanation: 'Radiohead library for this LoRa module to work' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: State true or false. Machine-to-Machine Interface (M2MI) is one of the major components of Supervisory control and Data Acquisition that is used for enabling control and operations of the remote processes by human operators.
questions.explanation: SCADA components listed: sensors, relays, telemetry units, SCADA master units, HMIs (human-machine interface), communication infrastructure (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control); no 'M2MI'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Zigbee uses the ______ standard for defining its physical and medium access control (layers 1 and 2 of the OSI stack).
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.15.4 (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: State True or False. The SIGFOX network can transmit up to 140 messages per day with a payload of 12 bytes per message.
questions.explanation: 'up to 140 messages per day, with a payload of 12 bytes per message' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following is/are false about the rule-based engine?
options: Extract causal and temporal patterns using predefined rules
Handles multiple data streams and correlates them to provide meaningful output
Cannot process data in near real-time
questions.explanation: Lecture stresses CEP must 'process the data in real near real-time' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1), so 'cannot process data in near real-time' is the false one.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Zigbee device type?
questions.explanation: 'A ZigBee module basically can be of 3 types ... coordinator, a router, and an end device' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: What is the role of message brokers like MQTT and Apache Kafka in real-time IoT processing systems?
options: They transfer data to analytical pipelines
They eliminate the need for data analysis
They reduce data complexity by deleting unnecessary events
questions.explanation: 'message broker such as MQTT ... or apache Kafka ... used to transfer the data to different analytic pipelines' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which type of analytics in IIoT focuses on forecasting future conditions?
questions.explanation: Predictive analytics outcome: 'forecasting for future conditions' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a key component of the Smart Water Management Platform (SWAMP)?
questions.explanation: SWAMP components (sensors, virtual entities, data management, analytics) per Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2; ERP is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a phase of Industrial Manufacturing workflow?
options: Collection of service offerings and infrastructure
Virtualization, allocation, and management of services
questions.explanation: Industrial manufacturing workflow phases: collection of service offers & infrastructure; virtualization, allocation & management; on-demand service provisioning (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a key component of SCADA?
questions.explanation: SCADA components: 'sensors, relays, telemetry units, SCADA master units, HMIs ... communication infrastructure' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a major component of an Industrial Control System?
questions.explanation: Four ICS components: process variable, set points, controller, manipulating variables (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic of Big Data Analytics in IIoT?
questions.explanation: Volume, velocity, variability, veracity, variety (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which software is commonly used for batch-oriented analytics?
questions.explanation: Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental type of IIoT Analytics?
questions.explanation: Descriptive, predictive, prescriptive (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which machine learning algorithm enables machines to improve their performance by automatically learning the ideal behaviors for a specific environment?
questions.explanation: RL 'enables machines to improve its performance by automatically learning the ideal behaviors for a specific environment' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following represents a key feature of Fuzzy c-Means clustering?
options: A data point can belong to more than one cluster
A data point belongs strictly to only one cluster
questions.explanation: FCM point may belong to multiple clusters, and is faster (not slower) than K-means (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the ThingWorx platform?
options: Has the ability to monitor the condition
questions.explanation: ThingWorx 'performs complex analytical processes, deliver real-time perception, offers the ability of condition monitoring' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: State True or False. Deep learning is an "end-to-end learning", which extracts features on its own. On the contrary, in machine learning, features are to be explicitly mentioned.
questions.explanation: 'Deep learning is an end-to-end learning which extracts features on its own ... in machine learning features are to be explicitly manually mentioned' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about machine learning (ML)?
options: ML is the subset of AI that can learn automatically from the object features
ML is the subset of DL which can learn automatically by finding the features of the object on its own
ML always performs better than Deep Learning models
ML can only be used for image recognition tasks
questions.explanation: 'machine learning focuses on learning automatically from certain object features'; ML is a subset of AI (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about MindSphere is incorrect?
options: Cloud-based operating system platform for IoT
Bring together IoT data from products, factories, machines, and systems to exploit its prosperity
questions.explanation: MindSphere 'is an open Platform-as-a-Service' (not safety-as-a-service), cloud-based OS for IoT, enterprise oriented (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is/are key characteristic(s) of a Consumer IoT cloud platform?
options: Provide very specific applications for end users
questions.explanation: Consumer IoT clouds: 'very specific applications ... modest levels of security ... very cost sensitive' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental cloud computing service?

To ensure that only new systems are implemented, not legacy ones
To increase the complexity of the smart factory floor

questions.q: In IIoT, where are sensors and actuators primarily used compared to traditional automation?

questions.explanation: L17: in IIoT, sensors and actuators are 'used everywhere to control, enhance, and optimize various functions'.

questions.q: In the mining industry, how do sensor networks with gas sensors, strata monitoring devices, and RFID tags contribute to safety and efficiency?
options: They only help in tracking miners' locations
They are primarily used for communication between miners
They replace the need for human inspection
They provide early disaster warning, monitor working conditions, and help locate miners
questions.explanation: L17: mining benefits are 'early disaster warning, working condition of the miners can be monitored ... Locating and monitoring the miners'.

questions.q: Who coined the term "Industrial Internet"?
questions.explanation: L18: General Electric coined 'industrial internet'.

questions.q: What are the three key elements of the Industrial Internet?
options: Intelligent Machines, Advanced Analytics, People at Work
questions.explanation: L18: intelligent machines, advanced analytics, people at work.

questions.q: In a milk packaging unit, how is flow measured?
options: Via a spinning impeller that sends signals when milk flows
questions.explanation: L19: 'impeller spins when the milk moves and sends the electrical signal to the control unit'.

questions.q: Which component is responsible for converting analog data to digital data in a smart sensor node?
questions.explanation: L19: smart sensor node has 'the ADC, the analog to digital converter'.

questions.q: In the context of the agriculture industry, what is the primary use of smart sensors like soil and water sensors?
options: To prevent patient falls in hospitals
For accurate use of fertilizers and determining crop health
questions.explanation: L19: agriculture smart sensors monitor soil moisture, water level, fertilizer and nutrition content.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Thames Water's smart water management system, as an example of Industrial Process 4.0 operation efficiency, primarily benefits from _________________.
options: Sensor-based equipment status monitoring and failure detection
Controlled power generation using weather forecasts
questions.explanation: L20: Thames Water example: 'sensor based equipment monitoring the status monitoring, detection of failures'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Interoperability in the design philosophy of IIoT for Industrial Processes refers to _________________.
options: Empowering smart objects to reduce human intervention
Virtualization of objects and digital models
Enabling smart objects to take independent decisions
questions.explanation: L20: 'Interoperability is about facilitating communication between heterogeneous objects'.

questions.q: In the 5C architecture of Cyber-Physical Systems, what does the "Conversion Layer" do?
options: Converts analog signal to mechanical action
questions.explanation: L20: conversion layer covers 'the conversion of the data into information, and its interpretation'.

questions.q: State true or false. In the case of spear phishing, the attackers send thousands of deceitful emails that resemble actual emails from credible sources while email phishing attacks are targeted to a specific person or organization to obtain sensitive information.
questions.explanation: The roles are swapped: spear phishing targets a specific person or organization, while email phishing sends mass deceptive emails. So False.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about the CIA triad in network and computer system security?
options: Confidentiality ensures that information is concealed and protected from unauthorized access
Integrity refers to maintaining the accuracy and consistency of data, and can always be violated by intentional attacks
Availability is compromised when authorized users are denied access to information due to network attacks like DDoS
questions.explanation: L16: integrity ensures data cannot be changed in an unauthorized manner. Saying it 'can always be violated by intentional attacks' is the incorrect statement; A and C are correct.

questions.q: According to the ICP DAS framework for Industry 4.0, under which category does "System health diagnosis" fall?
questions.explanation: Corrected after checking the lecture (was: Safety). Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): ICP DAS 'In the context of manufacturing, machine internetworking, system health diagnostics, system health monitoring, production efficiency'; safety covers plant safety, surveillance, info security.

questions.q: Kaeser Kompressoren coined a new term for their service-based business model, in which users pay per cubic meter of compressed air used. What is this model called?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): air-as-a-service, 'pay per cubic meter of air'.

questions.q: Which company is highlighted for its use of smart glasses for fault detection in its manufacturing process?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2) credits Boeing's smart manufacturing with 'reduced errors in the manufacturing process' (the smart-glasses detail is on the slide, not spoken); Boeing is the known smart-glasses user.

questions.q: What is a business model as defined by the "Business Model Generation" book?
options: The organizational and financial architecture of a business
The rationale of how an organization creates, delivers, and captures value
A description of how a business intends to earn profits
The network of suppliers and partners that optimize a business
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): business model 'captures ... the rationale behind how the organization ... deliver value ... capturing the value' (Osterwalder's Business Model Generation definition).

questions.q: Which IoT business model relieves the customer from the responsibilities of ownership and maintenance, focusing on a "Pay-per-outcome" approach?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): outcome-based = 'pay-per-outcome ... customer is basically relieved from the responsibility of ownership, and maintenance'.

questions.q: In a Cloud-Based Business Model, how do customers typically access services?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): cloud resources offered on demand/subscription, i.e. temporarily leased.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the revenue model in Service-Oriented Business Models in IIoT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): service-oriented revenue model: 'collecting and monetizing from the collected data directly or indirectly'.

questions.q: Which type of Cloud-Based Business Model aims at providing the required hardware and software online in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IaaS - hardware/computing infrastructure as a service.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA)?
options: Allowing interoperability and guiding IIoT technologies
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): IIRA applies 'to allow interoperability, mapping application technologies, and in guiding the use of these technologies'.

questions.q: An IIoT product is being tested in different continents for performance, standardization, and interoperability before its release. Which organization is most likely facilitating this?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): IIC testbeds, where innovations are 'rigorously tested ... before they are actually launched in the market'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a Lagging KPI for OSH?
options: Number of lost-time incident frequency rate
Percentage of managers with adequate OSH training
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): lagging KPIs: 'number of lost-time incident frequency rate ... number of fatalities'.

questions.q: In the usage Viewpoint, which element of an Activity defines the conditions under which the activity is initiated?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'Trigger basically are the conditions under which the activity is initiated'.

questions.q: In the context of the Usage Viewpoint of the Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA), what is considered the basic unit of work?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): task is the basic unit of work.

questions.q: Which of the following represents key feature(s) of the process-oriented business model?
options: Execution of various business processes within the organization
Presence of process owners to supervise the processes
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2) describes process optimization within/across companies; executing processes, process owners and process performance evaluation are all standard features, so 'All of these'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. __________________ is an electrical framework that provides two-way communication between the consumers and suppliers. With the help of smart meters, smart appliances, and energy-efficient resources, it efficiently delivers electricity to the consumers.
questions.explanation: Definition of smart grid (two-way communication, smart meters); Lecture 26 lists smart grid among IIoT applications.

questions.q: In the diagram for the manufacturing process, which unit comes immediately after the "Quality Testing Unit"?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): after quality testing 'we are going to have the counting of these different units of product', then packaging.

questions.q: The analog temperature sensor LM35 generates an output voltage that is linearly proportional to what temperature scale?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): proportional to Celsius.

questions.q: The MQ-2 gas sensor is specifically mentioned to detect the concentration of which gases?
options: Ozone, Sulfur Dioxide, and Nitrous Oxide
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): MQ-2 detects LPG, propane, hydrogen.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of an n-type MOS sensor when it is exposed to a reducing gas?
options: It increases with respect to the Baseline resistance
It decreases with respect to the Baseline resistance
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'In n-type sensors the resistance decreases ... with respect to the baseline resistance when ... exposed to a target gas'.

questions.q: According to the working principle of MOS gas sensors, what is the "Optimum Temperature"?
options: The maximum temperature the sensor can withstand
The minimum temperature required for operation
The particular temperature at which the sensor gives the best response
The temperature of the surrounding environment
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): optimum temperature definition.

questions.q: ModBus-TCP uses which protocol suite for data transmission?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): Modbus TCP uses TCP/IP and Ethernet.

questions.q: What does the acronym EtherCAT stand for?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'the full form of CAT is Control Automation Technology'.

questions.q: In the ModBus-TCP data frame, what is the name of the 7-byte header that identifies the Application Data Unit (ADU)?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'MBAP stands for Modbus application protocol header, which is of length 7 bytes'.

questions.q: Which variant of CC-Link offers the highest transmission rate of 1 Gbps?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): 'industrial Ethernet is 1 Gbps'.

questions.q: Profibus is based on which international standard?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Profibus 'is based on ... IEC 61158'.

questions.q: What is the Availability requirement for uRLLC?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): URLLC 'availability in the order of 99.9999 percent'.

questions.q: What is the end-to-end round trip latency supported by the Tactile Internet?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): tactile internet < 1 ms RTT.

questions.q: Which frequency bands are used by 5G NR?
options: Low band (< 1 GHz), middle band (1-6 GHz), and high band (>24 GHz) millimeter wave
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): 5G NR bands with high band > 24 GHz (mmWave); low < 1 GHz and mid 1-6 GHz.

questions.q: State true or false. The PROFINet protocol handles data transmission of large packets between PLCs and PCs, as well as enable integration with the Internet and Intranet through Ethernet.
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1) says Profinet is an Industrial Ethernet standard connecting controllers and field devices; Ethernet-based large-packet PLC-PC transfer with Internet/intranet integration fits, so True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. DeviceNet was designed by Rockwell Automation to enable communications between ______ and ______.
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): DeviceNet 'links different sensors actuators with PLCs' (designed by Allen-Bradley/Rockwell).

questions.q: Which modulation technique does LoRa use?
questions.explanation: Chirp Spread Spectrum (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. SIGFOX network give a performance of upto ______ messages per day with a payload of ______ bytes per message.
questions.explanation: 'up to 140 messages per day, with a payload of 12 bytes' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Zigbee Router and a Zigbee End Device?
options: A router can relay information to other nodes, while an end device cannot.
An end device is the root of the network, while a router is not.
A router can only connect to a coordinator, while an end device can connect to any node.
There is no functional difference between them.
questions.explanation: 'The router basically relays the information ... end devices ... no relaying' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: What software tool is used to configure Xbee modules before communication?
questions.explanation: XCTU (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which characteristic of IIoT data refers to the fact that it comes from heterogeneous sensors with different metrics, precision, and formats?
questions.explanation: 'massive polymorphism ... heterogeneous data ... different formats, precision levels ... metrics' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: What is the role of middleware in an IIoT system?
options: It is the physical hardware layer of sensors and actuators.
It is the final user-facing application.
It is the communication protocol for data transfer.
It is a software layer between the infrastructure and application layers that provides services and supports heterogeneity.
questions.explanation: Middleware definition (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which type of analytics answers the question, "What will happen and why?"
questions.explanation: Predictive analytics: 'what will happen and why' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1, slide label; narration slips the name).

questions.q: Which type of analytics aims to determine the best possible business decision?
questions.explanation: Prescriptive: 'the outcome is the best possible business decision' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: What is the primary goal of the FarmBeats platform?
options: To monitor the health of vineyards
questions.explanation: FarmBeats: data-driven precision agriculture (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: In the iRobot-Factory architecture, which component is responsible for cloud-based, high-performance, long-term data analytics using AI?
questions.explanation: All iRobot-Factory components 'interacting with this cloud based cognitive engine' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: In an Industrial Control System, what are the "Set Points"?
options: The standard values of process parameters for controlled operation
The values of process parameters measured by sensors
The process variables that are modified by the controller
The final output of the industrial process
questions.explanation: 'set points are basically the standard values of the process parameters for controlled operation' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a Closed Loop (Feedback) Control system?
options: The control decision is made without considering the process variable
It operates independently of the measured output
The control decision depends on the measured value of the process variable
It is not used in industrial automation

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) comprises of ______.
options: Processor unit, memory unit, power supply and communication modules
Sensor array, signal generator, analog filter, and PLC terminal
Actuator controller, logic gate module, and cooling system
Voltage regulator, touchscreen unit, hard disk, and keyboard interface
questions.explanation: PLC 'comprises of a processor unit a memory unit power supply and communication modules' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the DHT sensor in IoT applications is correct?
options: It measures only temperature and requires no external library.
It measures both humidity and temperature, and Adafruit provides a dedicated library for its use.
It measures pressure and temperature using built-in Python functions.
It measures humidity only and is used exclusively for industrial automation and does not need external support.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the role of a SCADA system in industrial processes?
options: It is only a hardware-based system for controlling pumps and valves locally.
It enables real-time remote monitoring and control of industrial processes using sensors and actuators, with data visualization through HMI.
It is a vendor-specific communication protocol designed only for power plants.

questions.explanation: SCADA used for supervisory remote monitoring/control with HMI, sensors, actuators (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: What is the goal of prognostic analytics in IIoT?

Inform about remaining useful life of an asset
questions.explanation: 'prognostic analytics basically inform about the remaining useful life of an asset' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: What are the three types of IIoT Analytics?
questions.explanation: Descriptive, predictive, prescriptive (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: What is a key difference between the process of Machine Learning and Deep Learning?.
options: Machine Learning uses neural networks, while Deep Learning does not.
Deep Learning requires the "Feature extraction" step, while Machine Learning does not.
Machine Learning requires manual feature extraction, while Deep Learning learns features automatically.
Deep Learning is a type of unsupervised learning only
questions.explanation: ML needs feature extraction; DL learns features automatically (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction, Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: According to the Venn diagram, Data Science is the intersection of Computer Science, Domain Expertise, and what other field?
questions.explanation: Data science = intersection of mathematics, computer science, domain expertise (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Supervised learning is divided into two main types of problems. What are they?
questions.explanation: 'supervised learning ... one technique is to basically classify the other one is to do regression' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: In Reinforcement Learning, what does an "agent" learn from?
options: An environment by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties
An unlabeled dataset with hidden patterns
A labeled dataset provided by a supervisor
questions.explanation: Agent learns by interacting with environment, which rewards or penalizes actions (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: How does the performance of Deep Learning typically compare to traditional Machine Learning as the amount of data increases?
options: The performance of both levels off at the same point.
Traditional ML performance continues to improve, while DL performance levels off
DL performance often continues to improve with more data, while traditional ML performance may level off.
Both show decreased performance with more data
questions.explanation: 'DL ... performance improves whereas ML ... will gradually come to a stagnation' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: The deep learning concept of breaking a complex task into simpler tasks follows what principle?
questions.explanation: 'deep learning also follows the concept of nested hierarchy. And it makes the complex tasks into simpler tasks' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about MindSphere is false?
options: It is a cloud-based operating system platform for IoT.
It is an open platform-as-a-service that integrates with AWS.
It is a mobile app used only for home automation.
questions.explanation: MindSphere: cloud-based OS for IoT, open PaaS with AWS, enterprise oriented (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: What is a major reason for needing cloud computing in IIoT?
options: To decrease the number of connected devices.
To handle the huge amount of unorganized and heterogeneous data, including data from M2M sensors.
To ensure all data has the same quality.
To reduce the need for networking
questions.explanation: IIoT data is unstructured, heterogeneous machine/sensor data in huge volumes (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which IIoT platform, offered by a software firm, provides a storage service called C3 Data Lake for unstructured data?
questions.explanation: 'stored in something called the C3 Data Lake' (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a good SLA?
questions.explanation: Good SLA: quantifiable, mutually acceptable ... (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following represents the characteristics of a good SLA?
questions.explanation: Achievable, meaningful, quantifiable, controllable, mutually acceptable, affordable (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: State true or false. Based on the application type, two popular types of deep learning methods are convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs).
questions.explanation: Not in the original lectures; CNNs (spatial/image) and RNNs (sequential) are the two standard DL families by application type.

questions.q: Which of the following are the key characteristics that classify data as Big Data in IoT applications?
questions.explanation: Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction lists volume, velocity, variability, veracity, variety; (b) is the only option made of big-data V's.

questions.q: In the Fog Computing architecture for IIoT, where are the Fog Devices located?

As part of the Industrial End Devices.
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): fog layer sits between the edge devices and the cloud.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a fog platform provider?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): providers FogHorn, Nebbiolo, Crosser, Sonm - not Sony.

questions.q: Which command in R programming is used to see the list of reserved words like "if", "else", "TRUE", and "NULL"?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'if you type in question mark reserved or help reserved ... you are going to get these reserved words'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a data structure in Julia programming?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): Julia data structures shown: tuples, dictionaries, arrays.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT fall under the essential characteristics of cloud computing according to NIST?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): NIST characteristics on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT represent a NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): NoSQL = key-value, column-oriented, document-oriented; relational tables use SQL.

questions.q: State true or false. In Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), the Namenode stores the actual data blocks, while Datanodes maintain the metadata information about the files.
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'name node ... maintains all this meta data ... data nodes ... store the actual data' - reversed, so False.

questions.q: Which property of a DCN refers to its ability to support any service on any server at any time?
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks): 'agility property means that a data centre network should be able to provide any kind of service on any server at any time'.

questions.q: What is the main architectural difference between the DCell/BCube topologies and the traditional Three-Tier topology?

DCell and BCube are switch-centric, while the Three-Tier topology is servercentric.
DCell and BCube use a single core switch, creating a single point of failure.
The Three-Tier topology provides better server-to-server bandwidth.

questions.q: What is the core principle of a Software-Defined Data Center (SDDC)?

The data center infrastructure is virtualized and abstracted from the underlying hardware.
The control and data planes are tightly coupled within the hardware.

questions.q: In Industry 4.0, why is Big Data analytics essential for handling the huge amount of data generated by IoT devices and sensors?

To store data only in traditional relational databases
To extract actionable insights for predictive maintenance, process optimization, and quality control
To eliminate the need for cloud and fog computing in smart factories

questions.q: State true or false. The main role of uSDN in the SD-6TISCH protocol stack is to minimize control overhead.

questions.q: In SD-IIoT (Software Defined Industrial IoT) Architecture, network monitoring is performed by which of the following component?

questions.q: What are the basic goals of information security?

Decrease scalability, interoperability, and real-time performance
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): 'basic security goals ... availability ... integrity ... confidentiality'.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the "Resilience" aspect of a Trustworthy IIoT system?

Protecting the system from unauthorized access, modification, and destruction
Ability of the system to function correctly under dynamic adversarial conditions
Restriction on data access - who can access and by whom it can be disclosed
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): 'Resilience ... system is able to function correctly on ... dynamic adversarial conditions'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a security requirement for Cloud Complied IIoT?

Data from thousands of devices stored in the cloud
Third-party services with trust-boundaries for security and privacy
Completely eliminating the need to safeguard control systems from incoming cloud information flow
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): cloud is third party - extend trust boundaries and 'safeguard the control systems ... from the incoming cloud information flow'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about the protection of fog devices in IIoT?

Standard cryptographic protocols are used for authentication between fog devices and the cloud.
Lightweight cryptography is recommended for authenticating end devices.
Fog devices serve only as storage units without computing capability.

questions.q: Which of the following standards is specifically associated with industrial automation and control systems security (OT security)?

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect about the security requirements in Healthcare IoT?

Communication data is secured using techniques like ciphering and hashing.
Data stored in the cloud may be protected with access control lists, signatures, and digital certificates.
Security management in Healthcare IoT completely avoids cloud involvement to minimize risks.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a Smart Factory?

questions.q: What is the utility of Dexcom?
options: To monitor oxygen saturation in patients
To measure and track blood pressure remotely
To monitor glucose levels continuously and notify abnormalities
To detect asthma symptoms using inhalers
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide: Dexcom continuous glucose monitoring; 'It notifies the doctors and patients if any abnormal situation occur'.

questions.q: Which of the following represents an IoT-based blood pressure monitoring system?
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide: 'iHealth BP5 is IoT based blood [pressure] monitoring system'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key security requirement in IIoT healthcare?
options: Cloud storage, Big Data, Sensors, Networks
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide 'IIoT Healthcare Security Requirement': Confidentiality, Integrity, Authentication, Availability.

questions.q: What is a major benefit of a digital power plant using IIoT?
options: Turbine's performance improvement and remote monitoring
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants' slide benefits of digital power plant: 'Turbine's performance improvement, remote monitoring'.

questions.q: Which network is primarily used for in-home IoT devices in a smart grid?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants' slide: 'Home area network - Covers in-home IoT devices. Wireless: Zigbee, 6LowPan'.

questions.q: Which component of the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) is responsible for analyzing the collected data?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants': 'the meter data management system (MDMS) ... helps in analyzing the data that are collected from these smart meters'.

questions.q: What type of RFID tag has an onboard battery but no active transmitter?
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': semi-passive tag has an onboard battery to power the IC but no active transmitter.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a key requirement for effective inventory management?
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': requirements for effective inventory management: meet demand, hedge against price increases, smoothen operations; increasing cost is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major limitation of barcodes compared to RFID tags?
options: Only one can be read at a time
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control' slide 'RFID tags over Barcodes': barcodes need line of sight, only one read at a time, less security and hence can be forged.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT represent a type of network security?
options: Detection of abnormal behavior by the network
Prevention of unauthorized sharing of sensitive data
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' network security types include behavioral analytics, data loss prevention, email security (phishing); HVAC maintenance is not one.

questions.q: What does "Integrity" in software security ensure?
options: Assurance of data accuracy and consistency throughout its lifecycle
Verification of user credentials before granting access
Extent to which software remains available during component failures
Prevention of phishing attacks via email
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide 'Integrity': assurance of uncorrupted data; maintain consistency, accuracy and trustworthiness of data over its entire life cycle.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a major risk associated with AR/VR in industrial applications?
options: Compromised content on the screen by hackers
Reduced risk of accidents and improved worker safety
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide 'Risks (AR/VR)': attacks by hackers, compromised content on screen, IP rights, privacy and security; reduced accident risk is a benefit, not a risk.

questions.q: Which of the following does not represent a typical application of analytics in facility management?
options: Determining exact square-foot utilization of office space
Enhancing real-time gameplay in virtual environments
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' analytics slide: energy consumption, data-driven decisions, cost optimization, remote monitoring, exact square-foot utilization; gameplay is unrelated.

questions.q: Which is a key benefit of IoT-based facility management?
options: Real-time tracking and better customer experience
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' benefits slide: improve customer experience, prevent unauthorized access, real-time tracking.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. ______ is one of the examples of the IoT-based body temperature monitoring device that takes into account the age, temperature, and symptoms of the patient to provide suggestions for the appropriate medicines or alert doctors.
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare': Kinsa smart thermometer is the IoT body-temperature monitoring device (others are glucose, BP, ECG devices).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a benefit of using IoT in the oil and gas industry?
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' benefits: production efficiency, save cost and time, improve asset maintenance; unlimited oil reserves is not a benefit.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a direct benefit of predictive maintenance using IoT in chemical industries?
options: Improve quality by efficient IoT analytics programs
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Predictive maintenance': reduce breakdown, efficient maintenance, improve quality by IoT analytics; increased energy prices is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a feature of IoT-enabled logistics improvement in the chemical industry?
options: Ensuring product location using sensors or RFID tags
Random manual checks without sensor support
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Improve Logistics': product location via sensors/RFID, track assets, detect contamination, alerts, warehouse monitoring.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes condition-based monitoring in IoT-based chemical industries?
options: Predicting quality by continuous monitoring and analyzing factors such as water, nutrients, and pesticides.
Running manual quality inspections once a year.
Ignoring environmental factors like weather and focusing only on sales data.
Setting random pricing models without data-driven insights.
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Condition-based monitoring': 'Predict quality by continuous monitoring; Water, nutrients, and pesticides analysis'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a way IoT helps minimize supply chain risks in the chemical industry?
options: Conducting only annual manual audits of warehouses
Real-time monitoring of equipment, materials, processes, environment, and workers
Ignoring process data and focusing only on final product delivery
Depending solely on human inspections without sensors
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide 'Minimize Supply Chain Risk': real-time monitor of equipment, material, environment, process, workers.

questions.q: What function does the IoT play in the pharmaceutical industry related to drug safety?
options: Detecting adverse drug reactions and allergens
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide: detect ADR, excipient effects, allergies.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the key features of sixth-generation drone technology?
options: Platform and payload adaptability, automated safety modes, intelligent piloting models and full autonomy, airspace awareness
Manual flight control with static camera mount and basic video recording
Single-axis gimbal with limited flight time and analog signal transmission
Pre-programmed routes with no adaptability and no safety protocols
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' generations slide: Sixth - 'Improved safety and regulatory, platform and payload adaptability, automated safety modes, intelligent piloting models and full autonomy, airspace awareness'.

questions.q: State true or false - UAV-based light displays are generally more expensive than traditional firework displays and cannot be reused.
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' entertainment slide: UAV light displays are 'cheaper and more exciting than traditional firework display'.

questions.q: How are UAVs primarily used in precision forestry applications?
options: To measure canopy height, density and volume estimation
To increase cost of forest maintanace
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' forestry slide: 'Measurement of canopy height, density and volume estimation'.

questions.q: State true or false. One of the applications of UAVs in telecommunication is to perform tower inspection.
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' telecom slide: 'Tower inspection by UAVs'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an application of UAVs in delivery and healthcare?
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' slide 'Delivery and Healthcare': 'Transport blood samples to laboratories for testing crucial diseases'.

questions.q: Which of the following activities can be performed by using UAVs in the mining?
options: Regular surface survey for optimized blast design
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' slide 'Application in Mining': regular surface survey for optimized blast design, manage stockpiles, site exploration.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a reason why case studies are necessary?
options: Enable detailed quantitative and qualitative analysis
Guarantee faster industrial automation by themselves
questions.explanation: L58 'Case Studies for Industry 4.0 & IIoT' slide lists in-depth knowledge/clarity, real-life phenomenon, quantitative & qualitative analysis; 'guarantee faster automation' is not listed.

questions.q: Which of the following is not typically part of a case study subject matter?
questions.explanation: L58 'Case Studies for Industry 4.0 & IIoT' slide: subject is 'a small geographical area or a very limited number of individuals'; national policies are not.
